namespace Mathoverflow486451

/-- There exists a semiring with a unique left maximal ideal but more than one right maximal ideals. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 16]
theorem exists_semiring_unique_left_maximal_not_unique_right_maximal :
    ∃ (R : Type) (_ : Semiring R), (∃! I : Ideal R, I.IsMaximal) ∧
      ∃ I J : Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ, I.IsMaximal ∧ J.IsMaximal ∧ I ≠ J := by
  sorry

/-- There exists a semiring with a unique left maximal ideal and a unique right maximal ideal
which are not the same as sets.

This has been shown by Goran Žužić and Moritz Firsching using an experimental pipeline:
An example is the monoid algebra of the monoid of maps from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$
over $\mathbb{N}$.
 -/
@[category research solved, AMS 16, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/f7502b9ed3e32d193ab8fee53d2e28f7d67f2dc3/FormalConjectures/Mathoverflow/486451.lean#L333"]
theorem exists_semiring_unique_left_right_maximal_ne :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ (R : Type) (_ : Semiring R) (hI : ∃! I : Ideal R, I.IsMaximal)
      (hJ : ∃! J : Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ, J.IsMaximal),
        (hI.choose : Set R) ≠ MulOpposite.op ⁻¹' hJ.choose := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow486451

reformulations.difference: Right ideals are represented by left ideals of the opposite semiring, `Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ`, rather than by right ideals with carriers directly in R.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The map J ↦ MulOpposite.op ⁻¹' (J : Set Rᵐᵒᵖ) is an order isomorphism from Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ to RightIdeal R. It therefore preserves maximal proper ideals and distinctness. A full equivalence with the direct-right-ideal formulation was proved as Review486451.first_statement_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The unique maximal ideals are selected using `hI.choose` and `hJ.choose`, and their underlying sets are compared after pulling the opposite-semiring ideal back along `MulOpposite.op`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: ExistsUnique supplies an actual maximal ideal and identifies every other maximal ideal with it; choose_spec ensures that the selected witnesses have these properties. Transporting the right witness through the order isomorphism above gives precisely its underlying subset of R. Thus the statement is equivalent to the existence of explicit unique maximal left and right ideals with unequal carriers. `answer(True)` has the affirmative polarity of the source’s existence question. The full equivalence was proved as Review486451.second_statement_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully express the two existence questions in the source. Boundary checks establish that existence of a maximal ideal forces 0 ≠ 1, so no Nontrivial hypothesis is missing; trivial semirings cannot supply witnesses. Independent tests also reproduce the source’s example that ℕ \ {1} is the unique maximal ideal of ℕ whereas 2ℕ is not maximal. The scratch file compiles, and its equivalence and test lemmas have no sorryAx dependencies. The source explicitly confirms the second declaration’s positive answer, example, and attribution. It does not separately substantiate the first declaration’s research solved tag; this is an unverified metadata point, not evidence of a status error. The second declaration’s linked formal-proof artifact was not inspected because accessing that GitHub repository was prohibited; the MathOverflow answer does report the proof’s existence. No mathematical declaration remains unverified.
